instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE returning count per user_id
output: WITH counts AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) c FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id) SELECT * FROM counts WHERE c > 2;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE computing average referred_by
output: WITH avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(referred_by) a FROM referrals) SELECT * FROM referrals WHERE referred_by > (SELECT a FROM avg_cte);

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Two CTEs joined together
output: WITH a AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(referred_by) s FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id), b AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) c FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id) SELECT a.user_id, a.s FROM a JOIN b ON a.user_id = b.user_id WHERE b.c > 3;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Apply filters before entering a CTE
output: WITH filtered AS (SELECT * FROM referrals WHERE referred_by > 50) SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) FROM filtered GROUP BY user_id;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE then order by aggregate
output: WITH total AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(referred_by) s FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id) SELECT * FROM total ORDER BY s DESC;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Modify via CTE then select window rank
output: WITH base AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY referred_by DESC) rn FROM referrals) SELECT * FROM base WHERE rn = 1;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Recursive CTE to create a number sequence
output: WITH RECURSIVE num(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM num WHERE n < 10) SELECT * FROM num;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Recursive CTE walking a holiday-date chain
output: WITH RECURSIVE dates(d) AS (SELECT '2024-01-01'::date UNION ALL SELECT (d + INTERVAL '1 day')::date FROM dates WHERE d < '2024-01-10') SELECT d FROM dates;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE combining two aggregates in one pass
output: WITH agg AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(referred_by) s, AVG(referred_by) a FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id) SELECT user_id, s, a FROM agg WHERE s > 100;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Multiple CTEs chained (a then b referencing a)
output: WITH a AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) c FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id), b AS (SELECT * FROM a WHERE c > 1) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM b;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Set expressions inside a CTE
output: WITH c AS (SELECT user_id FROM referrals WHERE referred_by > 10 UNION SELECT user_id FROM referrals WHERE referred_by < 2) SELECT * FROM c;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE for deduplication using row number
output: WITH dedup AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY joined_on) rn FROM referrals) SELECT * FROM dedup WHERE rn = 1;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Recursive hierarchy emulating parent-child with depth
output: WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (SELECT id, user_id FROM referrals WHERE parent_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.id, c.user_id FROM referrals c JOIN tree t ON c.parent_id = t.id) SELECT * FROM tree;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Materialize then refilter a CTE
output: WITH m AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(referred_by) s FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id HAVING SUM(referred_by) > 0) SELECT *, s * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(s) FROM m) AS share FROM m;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Tally CTE feeding a LEFT JOIN to fill missing grouping rows
output: WITH RECURSIVE grp AS (SELECT 1 g UNION ALL SELECT g + 1 FROM grp WHERE g < 10) SELECT g, COUNT(t.user_id) FROM grp LEFT JOIN referrals t ON t.user_id = g GROUP BY g;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE with ordered window and outer filter on rank
output: WITH r AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY referred_by DESC) rk FROM referrals) SELECT * FROM r WHERE rk <= 3;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE used twice via self reference pattern
output: WITH c AS (SELECT user_id, referred_by FROM referrals WHERE referred_by IS NOT NULL) SELECT * FROM c WHERE referred_by > (SELECT AVG(referred_by) FROM c);

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Inline aggregate then filter in outer query
output: WITH g AS (SELECT user_id FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2) SELECT * FROM referrals WHERE user_id IN (SELECT * FROM g);

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Pivot-like pivot using multiple aggregate CTEs
output: WITH wide AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(CASE WHEN referred_by > 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over100, SUM(CASE WHEN referred_by <= 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) under FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id) SELECT * FROM wide;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Recursive CTE to expand an interval of ranges
output: WITH RECURSIVE iv(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM iv WHERE n < 100) SELECT n FROM iv;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE for lead-lag difference
output: WITH lg AS (SELECT user_id, referred_by, LAG(referred_by) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY joined_on) prev FROM referrals) SELECT *, referred_by - COALESCE(prev,referred_by) AS delta FROM lg;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Chained CTEs for multi-stage business calc
output: WITH step1 AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(referred_by) s FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id), step2 AS (SELECT *, s * 2 doubled FROM step1) SELECT * FROM step2 WHERE doubled > 20;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE referencing a correlated subquery
output: WITH big AS (SELECT user_id FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id HAVING SUM(referred_by) > 100) SELECT * FROM referrals t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM big b WHERE b.user_id = t.user_id);

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
Recursive CTE producing factorial numbers
output: WITH RECURSIVE f(n, fact) AS (SELECT 1, 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1, fact*(n+1) FROM f WHERE n < 10) SELECT * FROM f;

instruction:
Schema: referrals(user_id, referred_by, joined_on)
CTE on itself to compute growth from prior period
output: WITH p AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(referred_by) cur FROM referrals GROUP BY user_id), q AS (SELECT *, LAG(cur) OVER (ORDER BY user_id) prev FROM p) SELECT *, cur - prev AS growth FROM q;
